sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
In Mazy, the core gameplay mechanics are deceptively simple. You'll be presented with a maze, and your goal is to find your way through it by navigating through the labyrinthine paths. The game's controls are intuitive and easy to use, with the option to play with a mouse, keyboard, or touch controls. The game's physics engine is also remarkably smooth, allowing for seamless transitions and precise movements.

However, as you progress through the levels, you'll encounter a range of obstacles and challenges that will test your problem-solving skills and reflexes. You'll need to navigate through narrow corridors, avoid deadly traps, and use your wits to overcome seemingly insurmountable obstacles. The game's level design is clever and unpredictable, ensuring that even the most seasoned gamers will be kept on their toes.

One of the standout features of Mazy is its use of physics-based gameplay. The game's engine is incredibly realistic, allowing for a high degree of precision and control. This means that you'll need to think carefully about your movements and plan your route in advance, as one misstep could spell disaster. The game's use of physics-based gameplay also adds a layer of depth and realism to the game, making it feel more immersive and engaging.

The game's core gameplay mechanics are also augmented by a range of power-ups and bonuses that can be collected throughout the levels. These power-ups can be used to boost your speed, grant you temporary invincibility, or even manipulate the environment in creative ways. The game's use of power-ups adds an extra layer of strategy and depth to the game, allowing you to adapt your playstyle to suit the challenges ahead.
